title: 1960s Vintage Fashion Editorial
description: High-fashion editorial photography in 1960s style. Perfect for fashion magazine layouts, mood boards, and vintage brand marketing.

prompt.main: vogue paris 1965 fashion editorial photograph, elegant woman in tailored tweed suit and pillbox hat, dramatic studio lighting, contre-joupe pose, kodachrome color palette, rich saturated tones, art director richard avedon style --ar 2:3 --v 6.1 --s 750
prompt.negative: --no modern, casual, streetwear, instagram filter, flat lighting

explained.why: Magazine vertical ratio. Matches Vogue/Harper's Bazaar print layouts.
High stylize adds editorial polish. Fashion images need MJ's aesthetic sense.

tutorial.intro: Vintage fashion needs named era + named magazine + named photographer. Generic "vintage fashion" gets you Pinterest clutter.
steps: Magazine + year: vogue paris 1965 — naming the magazine anchors the visual style.
Outfit: tailored tweed suit and pillbox hat — era-specific clothing cues.
Pose: contre-joupe pose — French fashion term for "contrapposto", gives the body language.
Color: kodachrome color palette, rich saturated tones — film stock reference for color treatment.
Photographer: art director richard avedon style — name a specific fashion photographer.
tutorial.tips: Vintage = named era + named film + named photographer. Three named references = authentic vintage.

faq.q: Why does my vintage look like costume party?
faq.a: You forgot the photographer name. "Richard Avedon" or "Irving Penn" forces authentic period styling.

faq.q: How to get rich vintage color?
faq.a: Name a film stock: "kodachrome" for warm reds, "fujifilm velvia" for saturated landscapes, "ilford hp5" for B&W.
2:3 vertical is industry standard. Use 1:1 for Instagram reposts.
